titulo: Quiz — Nine seconds at a busy counter
subtitulo: Speak up, at normal volume, no padding
introPt: A crowded taco stand with no formal line. Listen for how the traveller claims a turn and orders directly.
cenario: A busy informal counter where speaking up, not waiting quietly, determines who gets served next.

dialogo.es: Deme dos de pastor, por favor.
dialogo.pt: Give me two al pastor, please.

perguntas.pergunta: At a busy counter with no visible line, what actually determines service order?
opcoes: Who speaks up and makes eye contact
Who is closest to the register
perguntas.explica: Speaking up, not silent waiting, is what gets you noticed at an informal counter.
It states plainly that you are next.

perguntas.pergunta: Why avoid English-style padding like 'I was wondering if I could possibly...'?
opcoes: It reads as distance, not politeness, at this kind of counter
It's too formal for any context
perguntas.explica: Directness at an informal counter is the expected, comfortable register.

perguntas.pergunta: Where does this no-line counter behaviour NOT apply?
opcoes: Banks and government offices with numbered tickets
perguntas.explica: Formal queues still exist in more bureaucratic settings.

perguntas.pergunta: What volume is appropriate for ordering at a busy counter?
perguntas.explica: Normal volume with eye contact is the expected register, neither timid nor loud.
